relevance_note: Single case report of a GFAP-variant patient: "a de novo heterozygous missense mutation in exon 6 of GFAP (c. 1097A→G; p. Tyr366Cys)".
method_note: Hand-read single case report; JSON assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory and every span checked verbatim by script. Two in-scope persons: the index patient ('patient', rule 5) and one previously published person, 'ref [8] patient', from the Discussion sentence 'the causative genetic variant was identified as p. Tyr366Cys in only one case [8]' (variant and cavitation given, so in scope under v4). The Discussion also mentions 'the youngest case showing cavitation in MRI at the age of 10 months [8]'; the paper does not say whether this is the same person as the p. Tyr366Cys case, so no separate row was made and the age was not attached to 'ref [8] patient'. Inheritance left 'not reported': the paper calls the variant 'de novo' but does not state parental testing with the variant absent in both parents (rule 8); parents are mentioned only for consent, so they get no rows. Age at onset recorded as gestational age ('36 weeks of gestation', prenatal ventriculomegaly) with no ISO duration, since it is not a postnatal age. Several MRI findings (periventricular rim, thalamic atrophy, brainstem hyperintensity, extension of cavitation at 13 months) come from the Fig. 1 legend. 'His muscle tone was normal' (neonatal) recorded as excluded 'abnormal muscle tone' under D-27; limb hypertonia was observed later during follow-up, not treated as a contradiction. Brainstem hyperintensity not mapped to the medulla/cervical cord checklist item (medulla not named). 'Unable to track objects' not mapped to eye movement abnormality. Spastic quadriplegia mapped to spasticity, not to limb weakness. Raised intracranial pressure is implied only by the purpose of cyst fenestration; the hydrocephalus checklist item rests on the stated hydrocephalus. The paper writes the cDNA with an arrow ('c. 1097A→G'); kept as printed. No contradictions found.
